title: A month without plastic
summary: A family of four tries to throw away no plastic for thirty days and discovers how hard, and how easy, it is.
paragraphs: It was eleven-year-old Paula who started it. Her class had watched a documentary about plastic in the ocean, and she came home angry. "We throw away so much," she said, looking at the bin in the kitchen. "Let's try a month without plastic." Her parents agreed, mostly because they thought she would forget about it in a week. She didn't.

The first problem was the supermarket. Almost everything was wrapped in plastic: fruit, vegetables, cheese, bread, even some bananas, which, as Paula pointed out, already come in their own natural {{packaging}}. On the first shopping trip they came home with almost nothing. Dinner that night was rice and lentils, from the only shop in the neighbourhood that sold them {{loose}}, by weight, into your own jars.

They had to change their {{habits}}. Paula's father started buying bread from the bakery in a cloth bag. Her mother found a market where farmers sold fruit and vegetables without packaging, though it meant getting up early on Saturdays. They made their own yogurt, which was surprisingly easy, and their own toothpaste, which was surprisingly {{disgusting}}. Paula's little brother refused to use it, and the family agreed that some experiments were not worth continuing.

There were moments of failure. A birthday present arrived in a box full of plastic bubbles. The pharmacy had no alternative for medicine. And at a friend's party, Paula drank juice through a plastic straw before she noticed. But at the end of the month, instead of a full bag of plastic rubbish every two days, the family had produced one small bag in thirty days.

They didn't continue with everything. The homemade toothpaste was the first thing to go. But the cloth bags, the market and the jars stayed. Paula wrote about the experiment for the school magazine, and three other families decided to try it. Her parents still remember the most surprising {{discovery}}: the shopping took longer, but they spent less money, because they bought only what they needed.

loose.meaning: not in a package; sold in any amount you want

habits.meaning: things you do regularly, often without thinking

discovery.meaning: something you find out for the first time

packaging.meaning: the materials used to wrap or protect things that are sold
